## Findings

The crop/editor interface is a single-file Tkinter application — `scripts/manual_cropper.py` — backed by `work/manual_crops.json`. Everything UI-related lives there. No other files in the workspace define a Tk canvas, undo stack, click handlers, or disabled/loading state, so this is the entire surface area.

### Application at a glance

- `/Users/sinchunyeung/Documents-local/Materials/Phy/DSE/scripts/manual_cropper.py` — Tk-based PDF cropper (the only interactive UI in the repo).
- `/Users/sinchunyeung/Documents-local/Materials/Phy/DSE/work/manual_crops.json` — persisted marks; current state has `metadata: {}` (empty) and many questions with a single segment each.

### Keyboard bindings (lines 48–50)

```48:50:scripts/manual_cropper.py
root.bind("<Left>", lambda _: self.change_page(-1))
root.bind("<Right>", lambda _: self.change_page(1))
root.bind("<Control-s>", lambda _: self.save_marks())
```

- Only `<Left>`, `<Right>`, and `<Control-s>` are bound. There is **no `<Control-z>` / `<Command-z>` binding at all** — undo is reached exclusively through the toolbar button (line 64). This is the most likely cause of "Ctrl/Cmd+Z does nothing": it was never wired up.
- On macOS, Tk uses the `Command` key for accelerators. `<Control-z>` will not fire from the Cmd key; a `<Command-z>` (or `<Meta-z>`) binding is needed for the user-facing shortcut, and `<Control-z>` for Linux/Windows.

### Undo history / state (lines 332–339)

```332:339:scripts/manual_cropper.py
def undo_last(self) -> None:
    segments = self.marks["questions"].get(str(self.question), [])
    if not segments:
        self.status.set(f"No saved segments for Q{self.question}")
        return
    segments.pop()
    self.save_marks()
    self.render()
```

- `undo_last()` only `pop()`s the last segment of the **currently selected question** and immediately persists/saves. There is no command stack, no per-question history beyond "last segment", and no inverse operation — just destructive mutation of `self.marks`.
- `finish_drag` (line 381) re-saves the segment PNG and re-runs OCR+classification on every pixel of drag motion; there is no throttle and no way to undo a drag edit (drag re-mutates `segment["top"]`/`segment["bottom"]` directly at line 378 with no snapshot).
- `next_question()` (line 412) is auto-called from `mark_from_click`, so after each click pair the question advances; undoing the click immediately shifts the visible page away from the segment the user wanted to undo.

### Click / pointer handlers (lines 95–97, 358–412)

```95:97:scripts/manual_cropper.py
self.canvas.bind("<ButtonPress-1>", self.start_mouse_action)
self.canvas.bind("<B1-Motion>", self.drag_boundary)
self.canvas.bind("<ButtonRelease-1>", self.finish_drag)
```

- `start_mouse_action` (line 358) calls `nearest_boundary(self.canvas_y(event))`. If a saved/pending boundary is within ~12 px on screen, the click becomes a **drag**; otherwise `finish_drag` (line 381) routes to `mark_from_click`.
- A 12-px hit slop combined with no `cursor=` change means the user cannot tell click-vs-drag apart. Clicks near saved segments are silently swallowed as drags.
- `drag_boundary` calls `self.render()` on every motion event (line 379). On a large image at 2.5× scale this re-decodes the entire PDF page per pixel of mouse motion — a likely cause of "clicks unresponsive" / perceived lag: by the time the user finishes the click, the previous render has not finished.
- `on_mousewheel` (lines 238–247) returns `"break"` correctly, but `<MouseWheel>` is bound only on the canvas, not on the `preview` Label; scroll on the right pane is a no-op (UX, not a bug).

### Canvas / overlay (lines 83–89, 272–295, 319–330)

```83:89:scripts/manual_cropper.py
self.canvas = tk.Canvas(source_frame, background="#444", highlightthickness=0)
self.canvas.grid(row=0, column=0, sticky="nsew")
vertical = ttk.Scrollbar(source_frame, orient="vertical", command=self.canvas.yview)
vertical.grid(row=0, column=1, sticky="ns")
horizontal = ttk.Scrollbar(source_frame, orient="horizontal", command=self.canvas.xview)
horizontal.grid(row=1, column=0, sticky="ew")
self.canvas.configure(yscrollcommand=vertical.set, xscrollcommand=horizontal.set)
```

- Canvas `scrollregion` is set to `image + 16` (line 287) and the image is anchored at `(8, 8)` — fine, but `canvas_y()` (line 341) divides by `self.scale`, which is `2.5` in fit-page mode. So coordinates are stored in PDF space, not pixels. Easy to get wrong if a refactor accidentally renders at zoom != `self.scale`.
- `draw_marks` (lines 319–330) draws lines using `self.canvas.winfo_width()` for x-extent. On the very first paint (before any `<Configure>` fires), the canvas can be ~1 px wide and the drawn lines collapse to a dot — a transient unresponsiveness until the first `Configure`.

### Disabled / loading state

- Searched the entire repo for `state=`, `configure(state`, `disabled`, `busy`, `after(`, `grab_set`. **No matches.** Nothing in the UI ever disables a button or shows a "loading" indicator. The expensive operations (`save_segment_png`, `ocr_clip`, `update_metadata`, `refresh_metadata`) all run on the UI thread with no throttling, no progress feedback, and no way to cancel.
  - `refresh_metadata` (line 179) loops over every saved question, OCRs each segment via `tesseract` subprocess, and rewrites the marks file. On a populated marks file (current JSON has 30+ questions) this can take many minutes — and during it the canvas redraw from any pending event will queue, leading to perceived "clicks not registering" once the loop finishes.
  - `drag_boundary → render` (line 379) does the same on every pixel of mouse motion, freezing the UI.

### Most likely root causes for "clicks unresponsive"

1. **No `<Control-z>` / `<Command-z>` binding** (line 50 area). User reports undo "does nothing" — expected, because the shortcut was never bound.
2. **`drag_boundary` triggers full `render()` on every motion event** (line 379), re-rendering the high-res PDF page. Subsequent click events queue behind these renders. Throttling or only redrawing the overlay line would fix the perceived unresponsiveness.
3. **`refresh_metadata` blocks the UI thread** (lines 179–183) — no `after()`, no threading, no disabled state on the button (line 69) while it runs. Long-running OCR freezes all input.
4. **No `cursor="crosshair"` on the canvas** (line 83) and a 12-px hit slop on saved boundaries (line 356) silently convert near-boundary clicks into drags; no visual feedback means users think the click was lost.

### Recommended focused changes

In `scripts/manual_cropper.py`:

1. Add real undo: bind `<Control-z>` and `<Command-z>` on `root` (around line 50), and add an undo stack that snapshots `self.marks` (or the changed segment) before each mutation in `mark_from_click` (line 396), `undo_last` (line 332), and `drag_boundary` (line 378). Provide both per-segment undo and per-question undo.
2. In `drag_boundary` (line 379), replace `self.render()` with an in-place redraw that only moves the affected canvas line (track line ids) instead of re-rendering the whole page, and throttle to e.g. `self.root.after_idle`.
3. Move `refresh_metadata` (line 179) to a worker thread or chunk it with `self.root.after(...)`, and disable the toolbar button (line 69) while it runs: `toolbar.children["!button"].configure(state="disabled")` (capture a reference instead). Add a `busy`/`cursor="watch"` state during the run.
4. Set `self.canvas.configure(cursor="crosshair")` at construction (line 83) and shrink the `nearest_boundary` hit slop (line 356) or make it a deliberate "grab" cursor when over a draggable line.
5. Stop calling `self.next_question()` automatically after `mark_from_click` (line 412), or only do it on the toolbar button, so undo immediately after a click still shows the same question.

No other files need changes for the editor responsiveness/undo behavior — `manual_cropper.py` is self-contained.

The crop/editor interface is contained entirely in `/Users/sinchunyeung/Documents-local/Materials/Phy/DSE/scripts/manual_cropper.py` (Tkinter; the only GUI in the repo), persisting to `/Users/sinchunyeung/Documents-local/Materials/Phy/DSE/work/manual_crops.json`. Key root causes found: (1) no `<Control-z>`/`<Command-z>` binding exists — only `<Left>`, `<Right>`, `<Control-s>` are bound (lines 48–50), so the shortcut never fires; (2) `drag_boundary` calls full `self.render()` on every motion event (line 379), re-rendering the 2.5× PDF page and starving click events; (3) `refresh_metadata` OCR-loops synchronously on the UI thread (lines 179–183) with no `after`, no threading, and the toolbar button is never disabled — a long OCR run freezes all input; (4) `nearest_boundary` uses a 12-px hit slop with no cursor feedback (line 356), silently converting near-boundary clicks into no-op drags; (5) `undo_last` (line 332) is destructive, has no stack, and `next_question()` is auto-called from `mark_from_click` (line 412) so undo immediately moves away from the segment. Recommended focused changes are detailed in the report (add bindings + undo stack, throttle drag redraws, background OCR with disabled state, set `cursor="crosshair"`, stop auto-advancing question).
